document.title: Commercial planning: FY27 managed workspace rates

chunks.text:
[00:00:14] Morgan Chen: Thanks. The goal today is to choose which scenarios Finance should model. We are not approving a new rate card on this call.

[00:01:20] Morgan Chen: One sales request is USD 19 per user per month for the standard workspace service. At that price, what would we need to remove from the delivery package?

[00:02:03] Casey Brooks: First we need the hours per tenant. The approved general schedule is still USD 24 and the September USD 28 draft is unsigned. Neither of those facts supports a USD 19 quote.

[00:03:11] Alex Rivera: The subscription includes administration support. If you remove that, we would be selling a different service. Implementation effort is also separate.

[00:04:02] Riley Foster: Acme is at USD 21 under its signed exception. Customers ask why the saved global spreadsheet shows another number. We should make the customer scope obvious.

[00:05:18] Casey Brooks: Agreed. Acme does not create a precedent for Beta, and neither exception changes the global schedule.

[00:06:42] Morgan Chen: For the model, I will compare 50, 100 and 250 seats. I will keep annual billing constant so we can see the cost effect.

[00:08:06] Alex Rivera: Please show the cost of a second cutover. The current standard package assumes one production migration. We keep giving away extra weekends.
chunks.location: Lines 8 · [00:00:14] · segment 1

chunks.text:
[00:10:21] Morgan Chen: Could we label the nineteen-dollar option as self-service and exclude the managed support work?

[00:12:33] Casey Brooks: You can model it as a separate product hypothesis. Do not put it in the quote template or rename the current subscription before approval.
chunks.location: Lines 8 · [00:10:21] · segment 2

chunks.text:
[00:14:05] Riley Foster: What should Customer Success say when a renewal customer asks about the draft increase?

[00:15:17] Casey Brooks: Use the approved schedule or the customers current signed exception. For anything outside those terms, request a quote review.

[00:17:09] Alex Rivera: Delivery can provide a sample of eight recent onboarding engagements by Friday, with pilot and remediation hours separated.

[00:19:43] Morgan Chen: I own the scenarios and will circulate them on 9 October. Casey owns the margin check. No revised rate is approved today.

[00:22:18] Riley Foster: I will review the renewal tracker for exceptions expiring in the next ninety days.

[00:25:04] Casey Brooks: Finance still has not approved the September draft. Keep using the approved standard pricing framework until the formal decision.

[00:28:46] Morgan Chen: That is the action list. We will schedule a decision meeting after the cost review.

[End of transcript]
Fictional demonstration. No real meeting was recorded.

Acknowledge critical production incidents within one business hour during contracted support coverage.
Severity 1 means a production outage that prevents a customer from performing a contracted critical workflow without a reasonable workaround. Severity 2 covers material degradation with a workaround. A request to configure a new feature follows the service request queue. The duty engineer records the severity rationale and the customer-reported start time before triage.
The acknowledgement confirms an incident identifier, a named owner and the time of the next update. It does not promise a repair deadline. Coverage follows the customer's executed service schedule; a proposal or casual meeting statement cannot extend the support window. chunks.text:
Run a full backup every night. Keep the encrypted recovery copy in the designated storage location.
The production administrator checks the nightly job by 09:00 UTC the following morning. The protected set includes configuration exports, customer migration manifests and the support knowledge workspace. Personal downloads, cache directories and local browser profiles are outside this procedure. Encryption keys are held separately from the backup destination, with access restricted to the recovery operators.
Record the job identifier, start and finish time, object count and integrity result in the operations log. Compare the protected-object count with the preceding successful run. A variance above 10 percent requires investigation even when the job reports success. A missing or incomplete run creates an incident assigned to the duty engineer; retrying the job does not close the incident until the integrity check passes.
Keep fourteen daily recovery points and the latest twelve month-end copies. This retention schedule applies to operational recovery only. A customer-specific hold takes precedence and must identify the affected tenant and record class. Do not overwrite the only known-good copy while investigating corruption.

chunks.text:
Test a sample restoration every month and record the recovery result.
Use the isolated recovery tenant for the drill. Jordan Ellis selects a sample configuration export, one migration manifest and a support article without telling the operator which recovery point will be tested. Record both the requested recovery time and the most recent intact object timestamp; these measures answer different questions.
The operator restores the sample, checks a checksum or record count, and asks the service owner to confirm that the result is usable. Do not reconnect restored automations or send test notifications to customers. Store the drill report with the job identifiers and scrub any credentials from screenshots.
A failed test remains an open reliability issue with an owner and target date. The operations lead reviews it at the next weekly service meeting. Closing the issue requires a successful repeat drill, not a description of what should have happened. The monthly report lists missed drills separately from failed restorations.
Run the monthly drill during the second working week and rotate the operator so recovery does not depend on one person. Jordan signs the drill result before month end. Revision 2.0 replaces both operational clauses of revision 1.0.

chunks.text:
[00:00:19] Sam Patel: Our depot opening moved forward. Can we finish the migration before the October rota starts?

[00:03:20] Alex Rivera: The revised proposal mentions four weeks. Engineering has not committed. The earlier proposal stated six weeks and allowed time for identity remediation.

[00:05:02] Dana Lewis: We have the 100 mailbox list, but twelve shared mailboxes still need an owner. The archive vendor has not confirmed export access.

[00:07:18] Alex Rivera: Those are prerequisites, not small details. We can overlap discovery and training, but I cannot schedule the cutover until the pilot reconciles.

[00:09:33] Riley Foster: The commercial total is still USD 12000. Does the accelerated window add weekend coverage or remove anything?

[00:11:46] Alex Rivera: Neither is approved. The draft assumes customer approvals in one working day and a clean pilot. We need the delivery owner to accept those assumptions.

[00:14:10] Sam Patel: Please show the four-week option and the fallback explicitly. I do not want the depot managers to hear a date that later moves.

[00:16:52] Dana Lewis: I can deliver shared mailbox owners by 18 September. Archive access may take another week.
chunks.location: Lines 8 · [00:00:19] · segment 1

chunks.text:
[00:19:07] Riley Foster: I will mark revision two as under delivery review. We should not forward it as a confirmed schedule.

[00:21:18] Alex Rivera: Escalate the delivery commitment to the administrator and service owner before sharing it as confirmed. Include the open prerequisites.

[00:23:44] Sam Patel: Agreed. Keep the six-week fallback in the steering note and tell us what would need to be true for four weeks.

[00:26:03] Dana Lewis: My action is the owner roster and the archive escalation. I will send evidence to the delivery record, without passwords.

[00:28:39] Riley Foster: Alex owns the feasibility review by 21 September. I own the revised customer note after that review. No new price or contract term is approved here.

[00:31:09] Alex Rivera: We will decide after the prerequisites and pilot plan are checked.

[End of transcript]

chunks.text:
Run a full backup every night. Keep the encrypted recovery copy in the designated storage location.
The production administrator checks the nightly job by 09:00 UTC the following morning. The protected set includes configuration exports, customer migration manifests and the support knowledge workspace. Personal downloads, cache directories and local browser profiles are outside this procedure. Encryption keys are held separately from the backup destination, with access restricted to the recovery operators.
Record the job identifier, start and finish time, object count and integrity result in the operations log. Compare the protected-object count with the preceding successful run. chunks.text:
Provision a workspace account within two business days after approval. Account enablement requires the employee roster.
The service desk starts the clock when the request contains a manager approval, legal name, employee identifier, start date, location and requested access profile. Morgan Chen owns the queue; a named deputy checks it at 09:00, 12:00 and 15:00 UTC each working day. A request received after 15:00 UTC enters the following working day's queue. Missing details return to the requester with the specific field identified; the ticket remains open rather than silently restarting the clock.
1. Match the approved employee roster against the tenant directory. Check for an existing suspended account before creating a second identity.
2. Apply the standard employee license, require MFA at first sign-in, and assign only the department groups listed in the approval. Administrator access requires a separate ticket and a second approver.
3. Send the activation instructions through the approved onboarding channel. Never put a temporary password in a shared document.
4. Record the request time, approver, account identifier and completion time in the access register. A failed activation stays assigned to the service desk until the employee confirms a successful sign-in.

chunks.text:
Disable departing employee accounts within 24 hours. Revoke active sessions and retain the audit record for 90 days.
People Operations submits the departure ticket with the last working time in UTC and a manager's instruction for mailbox ownership. For involuntary departures, the duty administrator coordinates the exact suspension time with People Operations and does not notify the user beforehand.
Suspend sign-in, revoke refresh tokens, remove recovery methods and check forwarding rules. Capture the resulting directory state in the restricted access register. Transfer business records only to the approved custodian. A retention or litigation notice blocks deletion of the underlying mailbox, but it does not block suspension of access.
The desk lead reviews overdue removals at the end of each business day. The monthly control sample includes five completed leavers or the entire population when fewer than five employees departed. Evidence contains ticket identifiers and timestamps rather than copied employee messages. An auditor can trace each sampled account back to the roster and manager approval.

A1: Clause | B1: Commercial terms / operating instruction

chunks.text:
A1: Clause | B1: Commercial terms / operating instruction

Finance checks the margin effect using the current delivery estimate. Approval applies to the submitted quote version and expires when quantity, scope or term changes materially.
A4: DISCOUNT-03 | B4: No account owner may split a quote into smaller orders to avoid an approval threshold. Promotional pricing, additional implementation work at no charge and extended payment terms count as concessions even when the subscription rate is unchanged. Customer emails asking for a lower price are negotiation inputs, not approval evidence.

Prepare customer QBR notes by reporting weekly active users, licensed users and the reporting quarter. Compare adoption across periods without deleting historical observations.
Riley Foster prepares the first draft five working days before the review. Use the completed calendar quarter and show the metric collection window. Weekly active users means distinct licensed users with at least one qualifying collaboration event during the final full working week of the quarter. Exclude suspended accounts and test identities. This measure is not the same as the quarterly count of users who signed in at least once.
Reconcile the licensed seat denominator to the commercial register. Record the owner and date of every metric extract. Show prior-period figures as historical observations rather than editing the earlier QBR note. If a calculation or source was wrong, publish a dated correction that identifies the affected metric and period.
Gather open service incidents, implementation residual items, training attendance and renewal dates. Customer Success owns the customer narrative, Delivery validates project progress, and Commercial Operations validates any price or term statement. A QBR may record an expansion opportunity without approving the associated price.

Acknowledge critical production incidents within four business hours during contracted support coverage.

The acknowledgement confirms an incident identifier, a named owner and the time of the next update. It does not promise a repair deadline. chunks.text:
Run a full backup every Sunday. Keep the encrypted recovery copy in the designated storage location.
The production administrator checks the Sunday job by 09:00 UTC on Monday. The protected set includes configuration exports, customer migration manifests and the support knowledge workspace. Personal downloads, cache directories and local browser profiles are outside this procedure. Encryption keys are held separately from the backup destination, with access restricted to the recovery operators.
Record the job identifier, start and finish time, object count and integrity result in the operations log. Compare the protected-object count with the preceding successful run. A variance above 10 percent requires investigation even when the job reports success. A missing or incomplete run creates an incident assigned to the duty engineer; retrying the job does not close the incident until the integrity check passes.
Keep four weekly recovery points and the latest twelve month-end copies. This retention schedule applies to operational recovery only. A customer-specific hold takes precedence and must identify the affected tenant and record class. Do not overwrite the only known-good copy while investigating corruption.
chunks.location: Heading: Backup schedule and verification · paragraph 14 · segment 1

chunks.text:
Test a sample restoration every quarter and record the recovery result.
Use the isolated recovery tenant for the drill. Jordan Ellis selects a sample configuration export, one migration manifest and a support article without telling the operator which recovery point will be tested. Record both the requested recovery time and the most recent intact object timestamp; these measures answer different questions.
The operator restores the sample, checks a checksum or record count, and asks the service owner to confirm that the result is usable. Do not reconnect restored automations or send test notifications to customers. Store the drill report with the job identifiers and scrub any credentials from screenshots.
A failed test remains an open reliability issue with an owner and target date. The operations lead reviews it at the next weekly service meeting. Closing the issue requires a successful repeat drill, not a description of what should have happened. The quarterly report lists missed drills separately from failed restorations.
chunks.location: Heading: Restore drills and evidence · paragraph 19 · segment 1

chunks.text:
Provision a workspace account within five business days after approval. Account enablement requires the employee roster.
The service desk starts the clock when the request contains a manager approval, legal name, employee identifier, start date, location and requested access profile. Morgan Chen owns the queue; a named deputy checks it at 09:00 and 14:00 UTC each working day. A request received after 15:00 UTC enters the following working day's queue. Missing details return to the requester with the specific field identified; the ticket remains open rather than silently restarting the clock.
1. Match the approved employee roster against the tenant directory. Check for an existing suspended account before creating a second identity.
2. Apply the standard employee license, require MFA at first sign-in, and assign only the department groups listed in the approval. Administrator access requires a separate ticket and a second approver.
3. Send the activation instructions through the approved onboarding channel. Never put a temporary password in a shared document.
4. Record the request time, approver, account identifier and completion time in the access register. A failed activation stays assigned to the service desk until the employee confirms a successful sign-in.
chunks.location: Heading: Account requests and provisioning · paragraph 14 · segment 1

chunks.text: Exceptions: contractors receive a sponsor and an expiry date. Accounts without a sponsor do not proceed. If the employee's start date precedes the target completion date, the desk lead must agree a documented temporary arrangement with the manager.

chunks.text:
Disable departing employee accounts within 24 hours. Revoke active sessions and retain the audit record for 90 days.
People Operations submits the departure ticket with the last working time in UTC and a manager's instruction for mailbox ownership. For involuntary departures, the duty administrator coordinates the exact suspension time with People Operations and does not notify the user beforehand.
Suspend sign-in, revoke refresh tokens, remove recovery methods and check forwarding rules. Capture the resulting directory state in the restricted access register. Transfer business records only to the approved custodian. A retention or litigation notice blocks deletion of the underlying mailbox, but it does not block suspension of access.
The desk lead reviews overdue removals at the end of each business day. The monthly control sample includes five completed leavers or the entire population when fewer than five employees departed. Evidence contains ticket identifiers and timestamps rather than copied employee messages. An auditor can trace each sampled account back to the roster and manager approval.
